A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ORION study. Their complete main text and supplementary material are readable, and the methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendix sections can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot, few-shot, and test-time adaptation experiments across 11 datasets, together with SVD and orthogonality-weight analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds comparisons combining ORION with CuPL and ZLaP in Tables 10–11.

M1.justification: The class-name-only LoRA procedure, prototype anchoring, soft orthogonality objective, and encoder replacement mechanism remain unchanged. The CuPL/ZLaP integrations apply the existing ORION method without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 recognition datasets and retain zero-shot, few-shot, and test-time adaptation coverage. The additional CuPL/ZLaP comparisons use those datasets; removing Table 7's task-description column does not remove any evaluated task.

E2.justification: v2 adds CuPL and ZLaP as evaluated comparators, each compared with its ORION-enhanced counterpart in Tables 10–11. Existing CLIP/MetaCLIP, CoOp, CLAP, MTA, TPT, StatA, and SVD comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Previously stated splits, Top-1 metrics, shot counts, training settings, and StatA batch/stream protocols are unchanged. The added comparisons use existing backbone sizes—ViT-L/14 for CuPL and ViT-B/16 for ZLaP—without specifying a separate new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The SVD ablation, orthogonality-weight sweep, and EuroSAT geometric analysis are retained unchanged. Tables 10–11 add comparator integration results, rather than a new sensitivity, robustness, error, or component-ablation analysis.

E5.justification: Three-seed zero-shot reporting, five-seed/split few-shot reporting, and StatA task/stream averaging remain unchanged. The new CuPL/ZLaP tables introduce no additional seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Tables 10–11 report CuPL averages of 74.60 versus 75.38 with ORION, and ZLaP averages of 67.53 versus 68.91; ZLaP nevertheless declines on four datasets. Table 2 revises CLAP+ORION Food101 entries from 80.88 to 80.8 at four shots and 80.69 to 80.9 at eight shots, and corrects the 16-shot CoOp SUN gain from +0.7 to +0.1. Other precision reductions are equivalent rounding; the remaining existing results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the orthogonal Procrustes/SVD formulation, and the MLE/K-means interpretation through Huygens' theorem are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about class-name-only orthogonal text adaptation, its probabilistic interpretation, and broad plug-and-play usefulness. The added comparisons support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: New Appendices D–E explain ORION's complementarity with CuPL's LLM-generated description diversity and ZLaP's transductive updates. They extend the applicability interpretation to these pipelines, without adding substantive limitations or discussing the ZLaP dataset-level declines.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link to the abstract and briefly describes initializing CuPL with ORION's encoder and prototypes. Existing optimizer, learning rate, LoRA rank, training schedule, hardware, and prompt-template disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for CuPL and ZLaP and positions ORION as complementary to prompt augmentation and transductive text refinement. The existing related-work discussion is otherwise substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds short appendix sections D–E and a code sentence in the abstract, and changes Appendix A's wording from ORION 'fine-tuning' to 'pretraining stage.' The main narrative and section organization remain largely verbatim.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–11, removes Table 7's task-description column, resizes Figure 2, adjusts spacing around Figure 3, and emphasizes ORION's row in Table 9. The existing figures retain their scientific content.

improvement.justification: Tables 10–11 provide direct evidence for compatibility with two relevant text-based approaches absent from v1, strengthening support for the existing plug-and-play claim. The corrected SUN gain and added code pointer improve reporting. These are limited gains: the core method and theory are unchanged, and the new experiments provide little protocol or uncertainty detail.
